Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Call recap
- Scope: comparative reliability and SLO behavior vs hyperscaler inference endpoints (failover, rate limits, error budgets, throttling).
- Goals: validate failover behavior under simulated region outage, measure 95/99/99.9 latency percentiles under sustained QPS, and confirm error-budget handling for graceful degradation.

Key differentiators we discussed (summary)
- Redwood: unified runtime with automatic model fallbacks, prefix/KV caching, and configurable rate-limit tiers + dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
- Hyperscalers: generally good global fabric and scale, but opaque burst/throttling rules and less predictable cold-start behavior for larger open models.

Requested next tests (we proposed and you confirmed interest)
1) 48-hour canary: run 48 hours against a representative endpoint from your staging traffic (we'll do a matched baseline against a hyperscaler replica).
2) Failover test: simulate region failure and observe latency spike and route-to-secondary behavior.
3) Stress run: sustained ramp to your peak QPS to observe per-tenant rate limiting and error budget burn.

- A short comparison doc (attached): 2026-04-12-reliability-slo-comparison.pdf (SLO callouts, default limits, recommended config).
- A test script and perf harness (drive link below) and one-off access to a dedicated canary pool for the 48-hour run.
- A preliminary SLA language / sample contract to help procurement (DocuSign link Ill share once you confirm).

Hi Linda  answering your questions inline.

On Mon, Apr 13, 2026 at 09:08 AM Linda Park <linda.park@nimbustech.com> wrote:
> 1) Regarding rate limits: can you confirm per-tenant QPS and burst behavior?

- Redwood default (hosted): soft quota per API key that is token-bucket based. Typical default: 200 QPS sustained with 2x burst window for short bursts (up to ~30s) before smoothing or 429s are issued. For customers on Dedicated, we expose a capacity profile (e.g., 1k QPS reserved) with predictable throughput and configurable burst windows.

- Implementation detail: we do token-bucket per-route and per-tenant, combined with circuit-breaker at the gateway to avoid cascading failures. Bursts beyond bucket are either queued (short window) or rejected with 429 depending on queue length and configured SLOs.

> 2) Failover: how long to route to a secondary region on an availability zone/region degradation? Do you keep requests queued or fail fast?

- Failover behavior: automatic smart-routing detects region health via active probes and request latency. Typical detection + routing to next region: ~1545s for degraded region scenarios (depends on health-detection thresholds).
- Behavior during failover: by default we prefer graceful degradation  we attempt transparent routing to a healthy region (adds network latency). If routing would violate a configured latency SLO, we can be configured to fail fast. During Dedicated deployments we can enable cross-region hot-standby with sub-5s failover at extra cost.

> 3) Error budget: if we exceed the error budget during the canary, whats the recommended mitigation?

- Recommended: 1) auto-fallback to smaller, cheaper model variant (lower compute but higher availability) 2) enable client-side retry-with-backoff + limited queueing on the server side 3) route a share of traffic to a warm-hyperscaler fallback if you want an external safety net.

- Practical default: Redwood will implement policy to send 90% of traffic to primary with 10% to fallback for canary weeks; if error budget burn is >50% in a 24h window we recommend pausing aggressive traffic and running root-cause.
